post.0:
I came third with 56: I spent round I and most of round II as the table's piñata, with Cal's Help Yourself plus Reprise, Ben's free Con Men off Walk-In and then a Grifter through Tryout each stripping my whole pile, so I never held a contest when it mattered after round II's green. The comeback worked in pieces: Desperado made round III's opening Help Yourself steal 10, then Recruit a Member into a free Big Tent plus Promote of Cutpurse into Ben's Alchemists set up +8 at game end, and Demote pushing Old Maid into Dee's cult was a -7 swing on the leader. What decided it was the last four placements: Dee had Lie Low covering a 19-resource pile, took magenta and yellow for +20, then bought Extra Hand to land a minion after everyone, Shake Down took Cal's Loyalists, and she cashed 10 more. I chose sure followers over a red bid I knew three later seats could break, and that was right, but I was never in a spot to fight Dee's protected pile.

META: The contest-versus-spend tension is real and the last-seat puzzle in round III is the best part of the game. What isn't working is how much of the game is copying and stealing other people's stuff: copy chains (Echo into Encore into Con Men, Echo into Poach, Tryout into Grifter) do more than any printed space, and the player who holds resources early just gets stripped. Lie Low in round III is the one real shield, and it decided this game. First thing I'd change: stop On Recruit copies (Encore, Tryout, Greatest Hits) from hitting steal cards like Con Men and Grifter, or cap what a copy can steal.
post.1:
I finished last, 53 to Dee's 66, and it wasn't the engine that lost it, it was that every engine piece I built got taken off me. The deciding stretch was round II into III: my Walk-In flip of Con Men got copied twice (Encore, then Echo into Encore) to strip my pile, Ava's Shake Down took Roadie while I was empty, Desperado Crime Wave wiped my green, and then Cal's Echo-copied Poach took Con Men and Alchemists in one placement. I clawed back with Grifter through Tryout and Shake Down on Cal, and the last-seat green puzzle with Crime Wave worked, but I spent round III recovering instead of converting. My patient-engine style just doesn't fit a table where held resources and cheap members are the main thing being harvested; Dee won by Lie Low shielding a big pile in round III and Makeover choosing her contests.

META: The contests-at-round-end core and the last-seat puzzle are really good; my best moments were reading what the final seats could break with one placement. What isn't working is that theft and copying stack: Fence, Desperado, Echo, Reprise and Encore all multiply the same steals, so a cheap-engine builder is mostly growing crops for the thieves and the member market is as much a target list as a shop. First thing I'd change: stop copies (Echo, Reprise, Encore) from repeating member-taking and On Recruit steals (Poach, Shake Down, Con Men), or cap Desperado so it can't double into a whole-pile wipe.

I came second on 58 to Dee's 66. Fence plus Reprise on Help Yourself carried rounds I and II, two placements for 8 stolen resources each time, and I turned it into 20 bought followers and the Red prize twice. The game turned at the start of round III: Ava opened on Help Yourself with Desperado doubled to 10 and took my whole 8 red, red I had kept on purpose to win the contest. Meanwhile Dee sat behind Lie Low on 15-19 resources nobody could touch, used Extra Hand to place after the last seat, and took Magenta and Yellow plus 10 bought followers; Lie Low in round III was the quiet winner.

META: The contest-vs-convert tension is the best thing here, and the last-seat puzzle in round III is fun. What isn't working is that copying (Reprise, Echo, Encore, Greatest Hits, Cover) on steal and recruit effects is worth far more than any printed space, and steal doublers make holding a winning pile a trap rather than a plan. post.3:
I won 66 to Cal's 58 by owning magenta and yellow in round III (+20) and getting the last word. The deciding moment was buying Extra Hand on my second-to-last turn: it gave me a placement after Cal, the last seat, and I used it on Shake Down against him, which took Loyalists off him (-3 for him, +3 and a Guest Book +2 yellow for me) and still let me buy 10. Before that, Lie Low in rounds II and III was the quiet engine: with my pile untouchable I could sit on two colors while everyone else strip-mined each other. Taking Big Dilute and then Makeover in round III was pure denial, because either one in Cal's hands would have flipped a +10. I nearly lost it to Ava's Demote pushing Old Maid into my cult for an 8-point swing, which I never saw coming.

META: The contest-and-convert core works: every round I was counting which colors I could hold to round end and which were just money, and the final placements of round III were a genuinely good puzzle. What isn't working is that buying followers 5-for-5 or 10-for-10 beats almost every member on pure numbers, so members are only worth it for abilities, and the copy chains (Echo/Reprise/Encore onto Con Men, Help Yourself, Poach) do more than any printed space. The one thing I'd change first: stop copies from reaching steal-heavy On Recruits and center spaces like Poach, or cap them, so the round III swing comes from contest play rather than copy chains.
